wasabi.region: North America (also EMEA and APAC at the same rate)
notes: Unchanged since September: every value re-checked on 2026-10-23 against the sources below and found identical. Pricing page: Pay as You Go 'Starting at $7.99 TB/month', 'No fees for egress or API requests'. Pricing FAQ: '$7.99 TB/mo ($0.0078 GB/mo)' for North America, EMEA and APAC; egress policy wording (egress less than or equal to active storage), 90-day minimum storage duration, 1 TB minimum monthly charge and 4 KB minimum billable file size all unchanged. docs.wasabi.com lists no pricing notice newer than the May 2026 one (effective July 1, 2026).
Pricing page states pay-as-you-go 'Starting at $7.99 TB/month' and 'No fees for egress or API requests'.
Pricing FAQ gives $7.99/TB/month for North America, EMEA and APAC, stated as equivalent to $0.0078/GB/month.

Free egress is conditional, not unconditional. FAQ wording: 'If your monthly egress data transfer is less than or equal to your active storage volume, then your storage use case is a good fit for Wasabi's free egress policy.' Exceeding that ratio violates the policy and risks service suspension. This matters for any restore-heavy model.
Minimum retention 90 days on pay-as-you-go: deleting earlier incurs a Timed Deleted Storage charge equal to the storage charge for the remaining days.
Minimum monthly charge is 1 TB of active storage (10 TB for Cloud NAS) - you are billed for 1 TB even if you store less.
Minimum billable file size is 4 KB; smaller files are charged as 4 KB.
Reserved Capacity Storage pricing is derived from the $7.99/TB/month rate with term and capacity discounts; exact RCS rates are not published as list prices.

notes.text: October 2026 refresh (2026-10-23): every US East figure was re-checked at the vendor source. No price changed at AWS, Azure, Google, Backblaze or Wasabi. The only data change is Backblaze B2 storagePerGBMonth, null in September, now 0.00695 from the official pricing page. AWS republished its S3 price data on 2026-10-15 with no change to the Glacier figures used here.

AWS per-object metadata overhead for Glacier is still charged in October 2026 (re-read on the S3 pricing page 2026-10-23). Verbatim from the S3 pricing page: 'For each object that is stored in the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage classes, AWS charges for 40 KB of additional metadata for each archived object, with 8 KB charged at S3 Standard rates and 32 KB charged at S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or S3 Deep Archive rates.' At $0.023/GB-month for the 8 KB and $0.00099/GB-month for the 32 KB, this is roughly $0.00000021 per object per month, which is negligible per object but dominates cost for archives of many millions of small files.

AWS free egress is still 100 GB per month. Verbatim: 'AWS customers receive 100GB of data transfer out to the internet free each month, aggregated across all AWS Services and Regions (except China and GovCloud). The 100 GB free tier for data transfer out to the internet is global and does not apply separately or individually to AWS Regions.'

AWS minimum storage duration, verbatim: 'Objects that are archived to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval and S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval are charged for a minimum storage duration of 90 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive has a minimum storage duration of 180 days. Objects deleted prior to the minimum storage duration incur a pro-rated charge equal to the storage charge for the remaining days.'

The 128 KB minimum billable object size does NOT apply to Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive. The pricing page applies it only to S3 Standard-IA, S3 One Zone-IA and S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. For the two deep classes the equivalent small-file penalty is the 40 KB metadata overhead instead. Several third-party comparisons get this wrong.

Announced 2026 price change, Wasabi: pay-as-you-go Hot Cloud Storage moved to $7.99 USD/TB/month for all regions (North America, EMEA, APAC) effective July 1, 2026, attributed to increased costs for storage hardware, energy and data center operations. Reserved Capacity Storage pricing is based on the $7.99 rate with term and capacity discounts as of the same date. This change is already in effect as of 2026-10-23 and matches the live pricing page.

Re-checked 2026-10-23: no 2026 price change was found for AWS S3 Glacier, Azure Blob Archive, Google Cloud Storage Archive or Backblaze B2. Google's Cloud Storage pricing-announce page documents only historical changes effective October 1, 2022 and April 1, 2023 (Archive at-rest decreases in the us/eu/asia multi-regions and nam4/eur4/asia1 dual-regions, and Class A/B operation increases); it lists nothing dated 2026. Recorded as not found rather than as an absence of any change.

Unit mismatch to watch when modeling: Google Cloud prices Archive storage, retrieval and egress per gibibyte, while AWS and Azure price per gigabyte. Over a 1 PB 5-year model this understates Google's cost by about 7.4% if the units are treated as interchangeable.

The two cheapest headline storage rates, AWS Deep Archive and Azure Archive, are identical at $0.00099/GB-month, but their restore economics differ sharply: a full restore of 1 TB costs $2.56 on AWS bulk ($0.0025/GB) versus $20.48 on Azure standard-priority ($0.02/GB), before egress. Azure has no bulk-equivalent cheaper-than-standard retrieval tier.

Free egress is not free in the sense buyers assume. AWS and Azure both give 100 GB/month and then charge $0.09 and $0.087 per GB respectively. Backblaze gives 3x average monthly stored data then charges $0.01/GB. Wasabi gives unmetered egress only while monthly egress stays at or below your stored volume, and reserves the right to suspend service otherwise. Google publishes no free internet egress allowance on the Cloud Storage pricing page.

Method note: the AWS and Azure pricing pages both render rates client-side and serve placeholder tokens in HTML ('{priceOf!...}' and '$-' respectively). Figures here come from the vendors' own price data: AWS b0.p.awsstatic.com meteredUnitMaps (s3 map published 2026-10-15, s3glacierdeeparchive map published 2026-09-11, datatransfer map published 2026-09-16) and Microsoft's Retail Prices API at prices.azure.com. In October the AWS maps key rates by opaque hashes, so AWS figures were read from the AWS Price List Bulk API files for us-east-1 (AmazonS3 2026-10-15, AmazonS3GlacierDeepArchive 2026-09-11, AWSDataTransfer 2026-09-16), which carry the same publication stamps as the maps. No third-party source was used for any price.
